plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, and underbidding risks losing auctions you could have profitably won. With a value of $31, bidding exactly $31 maximizes my expected profit by ensuring I win whenever profitable and never overpay.

This is a second-price auction (winner pays the second-highest bid), which is strategically equivalent to a Vickrey auction. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly your true value, regardless of what others do. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth if I win with a high second-highest bid; bidding lower risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. With my value at $31, I should bid $31 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other rational bidders do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks losing money while underbidding risks losing a profitable win. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I will bid my true value of $46 to maximize expected profit.
